narration: You're already betting your job on your employer every single day. But millions of workers are quietly betting their entire retirement on them too — and don't even know it.
visual: Two coin stacks labeled SALARY and 401K on opposite sides, arrows pointing from both toward a company building in the center

narration: The average worker holds 14% of their 401k in their own company's stock. Financial advisors cap it at 5%. That gap is a $47,000 ticking time bomb sitting in your portfolio.
visual: Animated bar comparison showing 14% red bar vs 5% green bar, then a '$47,000 AT RISK' badge springs in

narration: Enron employees had 62% of their 401k in Enron stock in 2001. When it collapsed, they lost their job AND their retirement — $2 billion in savings wiped out overnight.
visual: Stock chart line crashing from $90 down to near zero, piggy bank cracking apart with a jagged fracture line

narration: Here's what makes it so dangerous — if your company hits hard times, your paycheck stops AND your retirement tanks at the exact same moment. One bullet, hitting you twice.
visual: Company building in center with SALARY badge top-left and 401K badge bottom-right, both connected by dashed lines, crack appears in building

narration: Log into your 401k right now and find your company's ticker. If it's over 5% of your total, move it to a broad index fund today — and it takes literally five minutes.
visual: Phone mockup showing 401k dashboard, employer stock percentage animating down from 14% to 4%, color shifting from red to green as bar shrinks

narration: Your paycheck is already your biggest bet on your employer. Don't let your retirement be a second one. Three steps, five minutes, and your future self will thank you.
visual: Person silhouette with green shield checkmark, three numbered action steps fading in: log in, find ticker, move to index fund. Bold CTA at bottom.
